doc.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025

title: Accompaniment during a bass solo
summary: He likes freedom and space during solos, and is open to helpful ideas from accompanists.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I can tell that that’s been an influence on you because you would play a melodic lick and then you’d play it again, and if you did it a third time you would like alter it a bit. As if twice is good, three times you better do something to develop it. Or – but I did want to ask in this particular gig during your solo the piano player was just hitting a chord probably every four beats, very quietly. I heard nothing from the drummer. Now I’m not sure if there was a drummer but the question I’m finally going to ask is what do you like accompaniment-wise when it’s time for the bass solo?

Sometimes I like not to be accompanied at all and that gives me total freedom. And guys I play with a lot will give me the freedom to do that. You know? And it’s up to me to make something happen. And sometimes I do and sometimes I need help and they’ll sense it and they’ll come back in, you know, on the bridge or something and, “Here we go, help Tony.” But a lot of times I’ll go by myself. You know I like of course to be able to hear myself, because a lot of times you play with people and they’re playing over you and it’s just hard to get your message across when they’re doing that, and they’re busy you know? So give me my space, that’s all. And piano players and guitar players are such great accompanists usually. You know they work a lot with singers and horn players, that’s what they do every day you know.
I’ve heard other bass players say the opposite. Like don’t you dare go to that hi-hat thing during the bass solo.

Oh yeah, well some guys are really sticklers on what they want to hear you know? I’m open. ‘Cause you could throw me an idea and that gives me another place to go. I go oh, okay, I hear that, I’m going there. You know? So instead of the old, you know, my bag of tricks you know okay well I’m going to throw this trick in here you know, so it’s nice sometimes to get a little bit of boost from somebody you know or a harmony. “Oh man you play too much of that” you know. “Here try this seven flat five chord” or whatever it is. You know? They’ll shove this in your face. Whole tone scale, something different, anything. So I don’t mind that as long as I can hear it and it’s a helper. But you know when you play with people a lot you get used to each other, you learn what to do and what not to do.
